businessModel: Free browser that promoted Comodo’s security products and Secure DNS
summary: Comodo Dragon was a free Chromium browser for Windows that added certificate checks and optional Comodo Secure DNS. Its last release, based on Chromium 134, came out in May 2025, and it no longer gets security fixes.
bestFor: Nobody new: it is out of date and unsupported

pros.title: Domain Validation
pros.detail: Marks sites with stronger SSL certificates apart from weaker ones.

pros.title: Comodo Secure DNS option
pros.detail: Optional DNS filtering against malicious sites, chosen at install.

pros.title: Chromium compatibility
pros.detail: Chromium 134 still renders most sites, though not newer web features.

cons.title: Discontinued
cons.detail: A Comodo forum thread says it is discontinued and has not been updated since May 2025.

cons.title: No security patches
cons.detail: Chromium 134 is far behind current Chromium, leaving known browser flaws unpatched.

cons.title: Unverified privacy claims
cons.detail: Claims that it is more private than Chrome come from Comodo’s own marketing, not independent audits.

faq.a: No. The last release was in May 2025 and a Comodo forum thread says it is discontinued.
Not recommended: it lacks security fixes from newer Chromium versions and fails on some websites.
An actively maintained Chromium or Firefox browser, such as Brave, Vivaldi or Firefox.

timeline.event: Forum thread reports the browser is discontinued

securityHardening: Sandbox exists but no patches for 17 months
